title: Hemoabsorption in Acute-On-Chronic Liver Failure
summary: Acute-on-chronic liver failure (ACLF) is a clinical condition that currently has no causal therapy outside of liver transplantation. ACLF is characterized by organ failure, such as cardiovascular, renal, and pulmonary failure, an increase in endogenous toxins that are normally metabolized and excreted by the liver, and an inflammatory reaction affecting the entire body. Our study aims to investigate the effect of a novel procedure, known as absorber therapy, on ACLF.
criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
ACLF with intensive care treatment and ongoing renal replacement therapy through an indwelling catheter, and indication for absorbertherapy
Exclusion criteria:
Pregnancy
Acute Liver Failure
